title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. M* = ⊕_{0≤i≤2n} M^i is a graded cohomology-like module (Weil cohomology of a smooth projective n-fold). Σ* ⊂ End(M*) is a graded subring, morally the algebraic correspondences. L ∈ Σ^2 is the Lefschetz operator (cup product with a hyperplane class). π_i are the Künneth-type projectors onto M^i. On earlier pages, conditions (1.1)–(1.4), (3.x) and (4.x) gave an abstract criterion for π_i ∈ Σ. The previous page shows that if w_i, v_i ∈ Σ and π_i ∈ some larger ring F ⊃ Σ, then the elements π_{2n-i} v_i π_i and π_i w_i π_{2n-i} lie in Σ and multiply to π_i and π_{2n-i}, by descending induction on i.

This page.
- (6.1)_i: L^{n-i}: M^i → M^{2n-i} is an isomorphism. This is hard Lefschetz. Grothendieck notes it already gives (4.1)_i and (4.2)_i, hence the uniqueness of the π_i in terms of the grading of Σ*.
- (6.2)_i: the inverse of this bijection is induced by an element of Σ^{-(2n-2i)}. This is the 'Lefschetz-type' standard conjecture: the inverse of hard Lefschetz is algebraic.
- (6.3)_i: purely algebraic reformulation inside the ring (Σ*, L), assuming the π_i ∈ Σ*. There exists w_i ∈ Σ^{-(2n-2i)} with (w_i L^{n-i} − 1)π_i = 0 and (L^{n-i} w_i − 1)π_{2n-i} = 0. That is, w_i is a two-sided inverse of L^{n-i} between M^i and M^{2n-i}, and π_i w_i π_{2n-i} ∈ Σ is the exact inverse.
- He states that (6.3)_i, independently of any ambient M*, implies (4.4)_i. Hence π_i ∈ Σ, and the π_i are unique for conditions (1.1)–(1.2) (the criterion of sections 4–5).

Then, returning to M* with L satisfying hard Lefschetz, he writes the primitive (Lefschetz) decomposition (6.4) for i ≤ n:
- M^i ≅ P^i ⊕ L P^{i-2} ⊕ L^2 P^{i-4} ⊕ …
- M^{2n-i} ≅ L^{n-i} P^i ⊕ L^{n-i+1} P^{i-2} ⊕ …

He introduces the projectors π_{i,α} onto L^α P^{i-2α} and π_{2n-i,α} onto L^{n-i+α} P^{i-2α}.

Purpose. This prepares the theorem on the next page: (6.2)+(π_i ∈ Σ) ⇔ (6.3) ⇔ Λ ∈ Σ^{-2}, where Λ is the degree −2 'inverse Lefschetz' operator. These conditions further imply π_{i,α} ∈ Σ and the π_i ∈ Σ as the unique family with the required properties. In modern terms: the Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) is equivalent to algebraicity of all inverses (L^{n-i})^{-1}. It implies algebraicity of the Künneth projectors (B ⇒ C) and of the Lefschetz-decomposition projectors. All of this is phrased in an axiomatic 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' of correspondences.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The decomposition (6.4) and the degree bookkeeping are correct: w_i ∈ Σ^{-(2n-2i)}, and in M^{2n-i} the component L^{n-i+α}P^{i-2α} is correct.

Minor: (6.3)_i only makes w_i invert L^{n-i} on the images of π_i and π_{2n-i}. The exact inverse in Σ is π_i w_i π_{2n-i}, which needs π_i ∈ Σ. The bracket 'qu'on suppose déjà les π_i ∈ Σ*' covers this.
The claim that (6.3) implies π_i ∈ Σ independently of M* relies on the section 4/5 criterion. It is consistent with the previous page's argument, but the step is only cited, not reproved here.
Notational drift: on the next page L ∈ Σ^{(1)} versus L ∈ Σ^2 here (a weight versus cohomological degree convention).

ideas.what: Hard Lefschetz (6.1) plus algebraicity of the inverse of L^{n-i} (6.2) as conditions on a graded ring of correspondences
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968, publ. 1969); Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Algebraic reformulation (6.3): existence of w_i ∈ Σ^{-(2n-2i)} with (w_i L^{n-i} − 1)π_i = 0 and (L^{n-i} w_i − 1)π_{2n-i} = 0
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity of the inverse Lefschetz isomorphism; criterion for B(X)
ideas.where_published: Equivalent statements appear in Kleiman 1968 and in Kleiman's 'The standard conjectures' (Motives, 1994)

ideas.what: The algebraic inverse of hard Lefschetz forces algebraicity of the Künneth projectors π_i, and their uniqueness
Primitive decomposition and its projectors π_{i,α}; next page: these lie in Σ when Λ ∈ Σ
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz decomposition projectors (algebraic under B); sl_2 / Lefschetz motive decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lefschetz; Kleiman 1968 for algebraicity under B
ideas.where_published: Kleiman 1968, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures'

ideas.what: Axiomatic framework: graded subring Σ of End(M*) with L ∈ Σ^2 ('algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge')
ideas.modern_name: Abstract Lefschetz/Poincaré-duality algebras; Weil cohomology with algebra of correspondences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (unpublished); later André, Kahn and others in motivic formalisms

missed.claim: The abstract formulation is purely ring-theoretic: (Σ*, L, π_i) inside End(M*), with conditions stated without reference to M*. It is an unpublished axiomatic precursor of later abstract treatments of Lefschetz-type conditions on algebras of correspondences. The mathematical content, however, coincides with Kleiman's 1968 published results.
missed.quote: Cette condition implique à son tour (indépendamment de la donnée préliminaire d'un M*) (4.4)_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mild historical interest: it documents that Grothendieck developed the B ⇒ C and Lefschetz-projector arguments in an abstract graded-ring setting in 1966-67, before the Bombay paper. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful working-out of known material: the Lefschetz standard conjecture, its equivalent forms, B ⇒ C, and the algebraic Lefschetz projectors. All of it reached print via Grothendieck 1969 and Kleiman 1968. Only the axiomatic 'Poincaré-Hodge algebra' packaging is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: 'Ceci implique déjà (4.1)_i et (4.2)_i dans (3.1)_i et (3.2)_i': 'dans' is likely 'donc'.
'en termes algébriques : Σ* muni de E [?]': more likely 'Σ* muni de L ∈ Σ², où on suppose déjà les π_i ∈ Σ*'.
'(conditions [?] i = 4, 5)' is likely a marginal reference '(cf. n° 4, 5)'.
'L'ensemble des deux conditions (6.1) et (6.2) équivaut ...' is correct; the struck-out word before it is 'Ceci'.
